class_name: 願望-働きかけ-テホシイ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Says you want someone else to act: 〜てほしい on the te-form, 〜でほしい after voiced ta-stems (読んでほしい, 急いでほしい). Teaching references treat it as unusable toward a superior, where 〜てもらいたい or humble 〜ていただきたい is used instead. Unlike もらいたい it also takes non-volitional subjects, so it can wish about events as well as people (雨がやんでほしい).

examples.ruby: 今度[こんど]こそ本当[ほんとう]のことを話[はな]してほしい。
examples.english: This time I really want you to tell me the truth.

examples.ruby: 休[やす]みの日[ひ]くらいは子[こ]どもと外[そと]で遊[あそ]んでほしい。
examples.english: I wish he'd at least play outside with the kids on his days off.

examples.ruby: 日曜[にちよう]の試合[しあい]、お母[かあ]さんにも見[み]に来[き]てほしい。
examples.english: I want you to come watch Sunday's game too, Mom.

patterns.usage_note: Frames the act you want as a favor you receive, so it presupposes the other party's cooperation and usually lands as a firm expectation (急いでもらいたい). It sits between casual 〜てほしい and its humble-polite counterpart 〜ていただきたい, and is natural downward or among equals, rarely upward. Because もらう needs a willing agent, the doer is almost always a person, unlike ほしい.

examples.ruby: 出発[しゅっぱつ]まで時間[じかん]がないので急[いそ]いでもらいたい。
examples.english: There's no time before we leave, so I need you to hurry.

examples.ruby: 君[きみ]にはもう少[すこ]し責任[せきにん]を感[かん]じてもらいたい。
examples.english: I'd like you to feel a bit more responsibility here.

examples.ruby: 毎朝[まいあさ]の練習[れんしゅう]には、遅[おく]れずに参加[さんか]してもらいたい。
examples.english: I expect everyone to turn up on time for morning practice.

patterns.usage_note: States a request as a favor received from the listener, in humble-polite dress: standard in business mail, notices, and speech to customers or superiors (書面で残していただきたい). It is 〜てもらいたい with いただく, and a bare 〜ていただきたい in writing reads as a firm directive, so 〜ていただきたいのですが and 〜ていただきたく存じます are the usual softeners. It also attaches straight to a ご/お noun with no て at all (ご確認いただきたい).

examples.ruby: 契約内容[けいやくないよう]は口頭[こうとう]ではなく書面[しょめん]で残[のこ]していただきたい。
examples.english: We would like the terms of the contract put in writing, not left verbal.

examples.ruby: 受付[うけつけ]で名札[なふだ]を受[う]け取[と]っていただきたい。
examples.english: We ask that you pick up your name badge at the reception desk.

examples.ruby: 新人[しんじん]には基本[きほん]から丁寧[ていねい]に教[おし]えていただきたいです。
examples.english: I'd be grateful if you'd teach the new hires carefully, right from the basics.

patterns.usage_note: Voices a wish to yourself as a negative question, usually that the event will happen (早く来ないかな), though with an outcome the speaker dreads it reads instead as apprehension (間に合わないかな). Unlike 〜てほしい and 〜てもらいたい, which target a person to act, it has no addressee built in, so it suits weather, timing, and luck. It is casual thinking-aloud; said within earshot it becomes a soft hint.

examples.ruby: 駅前[えきまえ]にもう一軒[いっけん]、安[やす]いパン屋[や]ができないかな。
examples.english: I wish another cheap bakery would open up by the station.

examples.ruby: 今夜[こんや]は雲[くも]が晴[は]れて星[ほし]がきれいに見[み]えないかな。
examples.english: I hope the clouds clear and the stars come out nicely tonight.

examples.ruby: 試験[しけん]が終[お]わって早[はや]く週末[しゅうまつ]が来[こ]ないかな。
examples.english: I wish the exams were over and the weekend would just get here.
